stories.title: Interpretability result: neural networks are not tangled knots
stories.summary: A new interpretability result is being called one of the most important in AI, suggesting network internals are far more structured than assumed.

top_posts.author: @nickcammarata
top_posts.text: interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came awa

top_posts.author: @deedydas
top_posts.text:
This is one of the most important results in AI, period.

TLDR: neural networks are not tangled knots (polysemanticity is wrong). You can study their own neurons directly, without first "unfolding" them with a second model. 90% of neurons in Qwen-32B have one job.

Nick Cammarata
